items.str: Sparse Attention for Long Documents
Ada Lovelace   Alan Turing
1  Introduction
Transformers [2] have become the default architecture for
language, but attention over long inputs is expensive. Long
documents pose a challenge for attention models because
memory grows quadratically with the sequence length. We
study sparse patterns that keep a local window and a few
global tokens, and we measure how retrieval quality changes
as the context grows. The method is simple to implement and
works with existing pretrained checkpoints. Long documents
